task: If I deploy a new recommender model via canary, what should I monitor to detect drift? Cite your sources.
final_answer: To detect drift when deploying a new recommender model via canary, monitor key metrics such as prediction accuracy, recall, precision, F1 score, click-through rate (CTR), and conversion rate. These metrics will help identify any degradation in model performance and assess the impact on user behavior.

# Model Monitoring and Drift Detection

Monitoring deployed machine learning models is essential because model quality
degrades over time. Unlike traditional software, which fails in obvious ways,
ML models can silently produce worse predictions while all infrastructure
metrics look healthy.

## Data Drift vs Concept Drift

## Canary DeploymentIn a canary deployment, the new model version is exposed to a small fraction
of traffic, typically 1 to 5 percent. Key metrics are monitored. If the metrics
look healthy, traffic to the new version is gradually increased: 10 percent,
25 percent, 50 percent, 100 percent. If metrics degrade at any step, traffic
is rolled back.

user impact.Shadow deployment cannot detect problems caused by serving the new model's
predictions (for example, a feedback loop where user behavior reacts to worse
predictions). It is complementary to, not a replacement for, canary.

## Rolling Deployment

Rolling deployment replaces instances of the old version with the new version
gradually, one at a time or in batches. Unlike canary, there is no explicit
traffic split; instances are replaced until all are running the new version.

## Popular Implementations

MLflow Model Registry is the most widely used open-source option. It
integrates tightly with MLflow Tracking, which logs experiments and metrics.
Models can be registered directly from tracking runs.
